setup.title: Claude Code setup
setup.intro: Claude Code reads your project, edits files and runs commands from plain English. Pick a route and follow the steps on your computer.
needs: A paid Claude plan: Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise. The terminal route also accepts a Claude Console account. [See current plans](https://claude.com/pricing).
A project folder to work in. Start with something small you know well.

sections.heading: Route A: desktop app
sections.note: No terminal. Best if you have never opened one.

steps.title: Download the app
steps.body: Open the [official download page](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-quickstart) and choose macOS or Windows.

steps.title: Install and sign in
steps.body: Run the installer, open Claude and sign in with your Anthropic account.

steps.title: Open the Code tab
steps.body: Click **Code** at the top of the sidebar. If you are asked to upgrade, you need a paid plan first.

steps.title: Choose your folder
steps.body: In the row under the prompt box, open the first control and pick the top entry under **Local**. Then click the folder control, choose **Open folder…** and select your project.

steps.title: Give it a job
steps.body: Type what you want in plain English, or use the three prompts below.

steps.title: Review the changes
steps.body: After an edit, click the `+12 -1` style indicator to see what changed. In **Manual** mode, Claude waits for your approval on each change.

sections.heading: Route B: terminal
sections.note: Same tool, run from the command line.

steps.title: Install it
steps.body: Run the line for your system. It shows no progress while it downloads.

steps.title: Check it worked
steps.body: Open a new terminal window and run this. It should print a version number. If `claude` isn't found, [fix your PATH](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/troubleshoot-install).

steps.title: Start it in your project
steps.body: Replace the path with your own folder.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: On first run it asks you to log in. Finish in your browser. You only do this once.

sections.heading: Your first three prompts
sections.note: Run them in order, on either route.

steps.title: Have it read your project
steps.body: Check that it understands what you built.

steps.title: Create its instructions file
steps.body: This generates a starting CLAUDE.md from your code. Edit it down to what matters.

steps.title: Give it a small real task
steps.body: Keep the first change easy to check.

code.text: Add tests for the main function

tips.title: Be specific.
tips.body: "Fix the login bug where users see a blank screen after a wrong password" beats "fix the bug."

tips.title: Let it read before it writes.
tips.body: On anything bigger than a small fix, ask it to analyze the code first.

tips.title: Break big jobs into steps.
tips.body: Give it a numbered list instead of one giant request.

tips.title: Use /clear between tasks.
tips.body: If you have corrected it twice and it's still wrong, `/clear` and write one better prompt.

tips.title: Review every change.
tips.body: You keep what you approve. Read the diff before you ship it.
